title: traffic-smoothing-and-elastic-latency-budgets-standards-2026
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary

This document defines the Traffic Smoothing and Elastic Latency Budgets standards for Redwood Inference. It codifies how services declare and consume elastic latency budgets, how the platform and edge routers should smooth traffic bursts, and the prioritized graceful-degradation actions when budgets are exhausted. The goal is predictable tail latency, bounded cost, and coordinated degradation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Audience

- Service owners and API authors
- Runtime and networking engineers
- SRE and incident responders

Terminology and core concepts

- Elastic Latency Budget (ELB): A service-level allowance of ephemeral latency headroom consumed when bursty traffic or backend slowdowns occur. Expressed as a rolling token bank (ms-seconds).
- Traffic Smoothing: Mechanisms at the ingress/router and client SDK to shape request arrival patterns to the serving runtime (token buckets, leaky buckets, request scheduling).
- Degradation Actions: Ordered mitigations (soft and hard) that reduce resource utilization or work-per-request to preserve core user experience.

Goals and constraints

- Maintain P50/P95/P99 targets while minimizing cost increases from unplanned autoscaling.
- Ensure deterministic, auditable degradation behavior when enforced.
- Provide primitives that work for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments without per-customer rewrites.

Scope

Applies to all externally-facing inference APIs (generation, chat, embeddings, reranking) and the Redwood edge/router components responsible for request admission and routing. Does not replace model-level quality safeguards (use Optimize/evals).

SLO surface and budget primitives

Each service must publish a Service Latency Profile (SLP) with these fields (YAML snippet in Appendix):

- slo_target_p50: e.g. 30ms
- slo_target_p95: e.g. 120ms
- slo_target_p99: e.g. e.g. 350ms
- baseline_qps: expected steady-state QPS
- burst_qps_capacity: expected peak QPS for short bursts (<= burst_window_seconds)
- elastic_latency_budget_ms_seconds: numeric token bank describing allowable extra latency (ms * seconds) per rolling window (default 60s)

Services must register SLPs via the Catalog service. The runtime will surface the active budget consumption metric: elb.consumed and elb.capacity.

Traffic smoothing semantics

1) Ingress-level smoothing (primary): The edge router implements a per-route token-bucket admission controller sized from baseline_qps and burst_qps_capacity.
2) Client-side smoothing (recommended): SDKs implement local backoff and jittered retry windowing to avoid synchronized retry storms.
3) Runtime scheduling: The serving runtime accepts admitted requests and maintains a short-term enqueue with priority buckets (see "Priority buckets" below).

Priority buckets and request ordering

- critical: control-plane and authenticated health checks (always admitted, rate-limited separately).
- interactive: user-facing generation/chat requests. Prioritized by user token consumption and route SLA.
- batch: long-running embedding or offline reranking; admitted only when ELB headroom exists or in background lanes.

Admission and rejection policy

- When token bucket empty: ingress will attempt elastic admission by borrowing against ELB (if configured and available).
- If ELB has capacity: ingress reduces admission rate by a smoothing factor (default 0.6) and increments elb.consumed accordingly.
- If ELB exhausted: ingress rejects lower-priority buckets with 429 and returns structured error with fields: {code: TOO_BUSY, retry_after_ms, degradation_hint}.

Graceful degradation actions (ordered)

Services must implement a degradation plan with clearly labeled steps. Platform will orchestrate the top-level decision. Typical steps (apply in order until SLOs are satisfied):

1) Response trimming: reduce max tokens or response length by a route-specific fraction.  (soft)
2) Model substitution: route to a lower-cost/latency model variant (e.g., quantized or smaller) with quality tags attached. (soft-medium)
3) Feature gating: disable noncritical post-processing (summaries, citations, n-best rerank). (medium)
4) Request sampling: accept only 1-in-N requests for non-critical clients. (medium-hard)
5) Reject non-interactive/low-tier clients with 429 and structured reason. (hard)

Each action must include an expected latency and quality delta documented in the route SLP. Example table: 

| Action | Expected p95 improvement | Expected quality delta | Rollback latency |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Response trimming (25%) | -60ms | -2% quality score | immediate |
| Model substitution (base -> quantized-small) | -150ms | -6% quality score | 100s |
| Feature gating | -40ms | -1% quality score | immediate |
| 1-in-10 sampling | -200ms (system-wide) | -90% traffic | 0s |

Observability and telemetry requirements

All services must emit the following metrics (names are canonical):

- slo.p50_ms, slo.p95_ms, slo.p99_ms (histogram/buckets)
- elb.capacity_ms_seconds (gauge)
- elb.consumed_ms_seconds (counter or gauge)
- ingress.admit_rate_per_route
- ingress.rejects_per_route_by_reason
- degradation.action_applied (labels: action, route, model_variant)
- model.variant_latency_ms (labels: model_variant)

Tracing: add spans for "ingress.admit", "elb.borrow", "degradation.step" with tags route_id and reason. Profile correlation IDs must be present for any request that experiences > p95 latency.

Alerts and SLO burn rules

- Alert: ELB utilization > 80% for 3m -> page on-call SRE and owner team.
- Alert: sustained p99 > target for 10m -> page on-call and open incident.
- Alert: admission rejects rate > 1% of traffic for 5m -> warn owner and product.

- Automated responses: the platform will engage autoscaler if ELB > 95% for 2m AND cost-threshold not exceeded.

Testing and rollout guidance

1) Unit test: validate SLP registration and expected admission gates with a mock router.
2) Integration test: run against the Predictable Cost/Latency simulator (see related pages) to assert behavior for 50/95/99 percentiles across synthetic burst patterns.
3) Canary: deploy degradation plan as feature flags; enable ELB borrowing only under canary route.
4) Chaos: periodic game-days injecting slow model backend and verify ordered degradation steps fire and recover cleanly.

Operational runbook (when ELB alert fires)

1) Pager receives alert; on-call confirms with dashboards (SLO heatmap, ELB consumption, ingress rejects).
2) Triage: determine if cause is external traffic spike, model backend slowdown, or infra contention.

- If traffic spike: temporarily increase burst_qps_capacity in Catalog and notify owner.
- If model slowdown: consider immediate model substitution or route to warm fallback pool.
- If infra contention: coordinate with SRE to identify noisy neighbours and scale cluster nodes.

3) If degradation actions are active, validate quality metrics (eval set) for impact; rollback any model substitution if unacceptable.

4) Post-incident: create a short incident summary with timeline, actions, and ELB meters and attach to incident tracker.

Change management and ownership

- Service owners are responsible for defining SLPs and degradation plans.
- Runtime/ingress teams own the enforcement primitives and smoothing parameters.
- SRE owns alerts, autoscaling triggers, and game-day choreography.

Appendix: Example SLP YAML

---
route: /v1/chat/generate
owner: team-conversation
slo_target_p50: 40  # ms
slo_target_p95: 140 # ms
slo_target_p99: 380 # ms
baseline_qps: 120
burst_qps_capacity: 800
elastic_latency_budget_ms_seconds: 72000 # equivalent to 1200ms for 60s window
degradation_plan:
  - name: trim_response_20pct
    type: response_trim
    expected_p95_delta_ms: -50
    quality_delta_pct: -2
  - name: route_to_quantized_small
    type: model_substitution
    expected_p95_delta_ms: -160
    quality_delta_pct: -6
---

Appendix: Example ingress rejection response (JSON)

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "code": "TOO_BUSY",
  "message": "Service temporarily rejecting low priority requests due to capacity constraints.",
  "retry_after_ms": 3000,
  "degradation_hint": "response_trim_active, model_substitution_active"
}
